title: India to Cut Visa Form Fields by Around 70% in Overhaul for Foreign Travellers
excerpt: The Home Ministry plans slimmer forms across all 22 visa categories from next year, dropping the 'district' field and letting tourists list a hotel as their local address.
body:
• India plans to cut the number of fields on its visa application forms by around 70%, across all 22 visa categories, a senior government official told The Hindu.
  • The 'district' field will be dropped, and foreign tourists will be able to give a hotel or guest house address instead of a local residential address.
  • The changes are expected to be introduced from next year; nothing changes for applications filed today.
  • For diaspora families, the practical effect is simpler paperwork for foreign-national relatives, spouses and friends planning trips to India.

India is preparing to slim down its visa application forms, removing redundant fields so that they match global standards, a senior government official has told The Hindu. The number of fields is expected to fall by around 70%, and the changes will apply across all 22 visa categories.

What is changing

"Visa forms will be simpler and more user-friendly in the coming days. The changes will be reflected in all 22 visa categories in line with global standards. The forms will be slimmer and the number of fields will be reduced by around 70%," the official said. The Union Home Ministry has convened several meetings on further liberalising the visa regime, and officials said the forms are being redesigned to eliminate repetitive fields that ask applicants for the same information more than once.

https://x.com/vijaita/status/2117808680242716814

Two changes illustrate the direction. The 'district' field will be removed because it has no equivalent on most other countries' forms. And the 'local address' requirement will be liberalised: instead of naming a resident contact in India, foreign tourists will be able to provide the address of the hotel or guest house where they are staying. The current e-Visa application runs to nine pages and asks applicants whether they have ever been involved in "cybercrime, terrorist activities, sabotage, espionage, genocide, political killing or any other act of violence."

Who this affects — and when

The overhaul concerns foreign nationals applying for Indian visas, in every category from tourist and business to medical and student visas. It does not change eligibility, fees or processing rules, and it does not affect Indian citizens or OCI cardholders, who do not use these forms. The official said the revised forms are likely to be introduced from next year. Travellers applying now should use the existing form on the official e-Visa portal and beware of lookalike commercial sites that charge extra fees.

Why the government is acting

The push comes as India's tourism industry presses the government to restore foreign tourist arrivals to pre-COVID levels, a recovery that has not yet happened. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha in August 2025, the Home Ministry said e-Visas are available to nationals of 172 countries and that about 95% of e-Visa applications are processed in under 72 hours. In August 2026, the government added 11 designated entry points for e-Visa holders, taking the total to 88.

What the industry is still asking for

Tourism officials and industry representatives have asked for more than shorter forms. Their requests include applying the 120-day advance application window uniformly across countries — for some nationalities it is currently 30 days — extending e-Visa access to Chinese travellers, and issuing Protected Area Permits and Restricted Area Permits together with the visa rather than on arrival. Protected or restricted area permits are required for Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of some other states. The industry has also asked for forms in languages such as Spanish, German and Italian, in addition to English. Those are requests under discussion, not decisions; the confirmed change is the slimmer form itself.
nri_angle: Simpler Indian visa paperwork for foreign-national relatives, spouses and friends of the diaspora planning trips to India.
